title: Star Cores: Spikes, Halos and Cycles (Cycles of Growth, Part II)
description:
Cycles of Growth, Part II. Every solid can be divided into pyramids, one standing on each face, with all their tips meeting at the centre; DICTO turned these pyramids inside out, so that each becomes a spike and the solid a star. The tips span a larger solid, the halo, and the tips of each kind of face meet in a core. This book follows the stars, halos, cores and cycles of DICTO's solids, continuing Part I, The Golden Cycle.

Five chapters, each a published paper with its theorems and proofs word for word: (1) The Truncated Icosahedron Star (#78): exact doubling and golden cycles of the TI Star, and its core, the TI Star core, alternating with the truncated icosahedron. (2) Star Cores of DICTO's Solids (#79): with each spike's tip at the pole of its face plane, the halo is the polar and the layer between star and halo is tiled exactly by one pyramid over each corner and one tetrahedron over each edge, for every convex solid: the thick form of Conway's join. (3) Core Cycles (#81): for solids whose faces lie on the axes of a regular solid and its dual, the core of each turn swaps the two depths, and two turns scale it by t²c². (4) The Gains of DICTO's Growth Rule (#80): the exact gains of every closed chain of DICTO's rule T, which explain the near-misses 4.944 and 11.542 of the TI Star. (5) Eccentric Pieces (#85): the valley law, by which the symmetric stars freeze while DICTO's sharp-edged pieces keep growing, and his notch pieces Maedate and Kuwagata for Kagemusha.

A card for each of 60 shapes (DICTO's 54 shapes of the studies, Cube Pearl, Golden Clasp, Hamlet and Ophelia of DICTO Solids v7, and the two notch pieces), with the solid, its stars and halo, exact data and the facts of every chapter; six plates; a table of every shape; a closing chapter with all cycles and chains in one table; index. New in the book, from its own runs: the treatment of Cube Pearl, Golden Clasp, Hamlet and Ophelia (exact chain gains 21811/11025 and (3715 − 1635√5)/36); Kuwagata's star solved exactly (it stops exactly at step three; the finished star has 122 corners and 200 faces, new within DICTO Solids v7).

131 pages. The cover is the STAR CORES square. The ideas and names are DICTO's. Computation and proof with Claude (Anthropic). Licence CC BY-SA 4.0. More at dictospheres.com.
